question: Does the ecology family keep reproducing at the history run's density of four members per site?
master_seed_origin: system clock at start; draw k uses master + k
script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Does the ecology family sustain births? Unselected seeds from the clock,
# four draws per cohort size, 256 members over 64 sites, 8 lineages, 96 ticks.
# Births = final stored entities - founding members - one world body per site.
set -euo pipefail
bench="$1"
master=$(date +%s%N)
echo "master $master"
for cohort in 32 1; do
  for k in 0 1 2 3; do
    seed=$((master + k))
    line=$("$bench" --ecology --seed "$seed" --population 256 --sites 64 --lineages 8 \
      --cohort-size "$cohort" --ticks 96 --output NUL 2>&1)
    entities=$(echo "$line" | grep -o '[0-9]* entities' | grep -o '[0-9]*')
    echo "cohort $cohort seed $seed entities $entities births $((entities - 256 - 64))"
  done
done
births_rule: stored entities after 96 ticks, less the 256 founders and one world body for each of the 64 sites; the dead stay stored, so this counts births
